# Synthetic test media

This directory contains the shared Go and browser media fixtures generated by
`tools/generate_test_media.py`. Run it from the repository root after
[preparing build inputs](../../docs/build.md#direct-go-builds):

```sh
python3 tools/generate_test_media.py
python3 tools/generate_test_media.py --check
```

Video generation requires an FFmpeg executable with `libx264`, `libx265`,
`libaom-av1` and AAC encoders. Use `--ffmpeg /path/to/ffmpeg` to select it;
`ANYKVM_TEST_FFMPEG` also sets the default. Audio generation requires macOS
AudioToolbox through the system `afconvert` tool. The default generates video
and audio on macOS, and video only on other platforms. No capture device is
needed.

Use `--groups video` or `--groups audio` to select one group. `--check` verifies
the selected files against `build/test-media.json` without running encoders.
Missing, modified or outdated fixtures are regenerated; `--force` rebuilds
them after an encoder upgrade. The 14 binary files, three HLS playlists and
cache manifest are ignored by Git. Ordinary builds do not require these tools.

## H.264 and HEVC passthrough

`internal/testdata/` contains two MP4/Annex-B pairs:

- `passthrough.mp4` and `passthrough.h264` use libx264 ultrafast/zerolatency.
- `passthrough_hevc.mp4` and `passthrough.hevc` use libx265 ultrafast with one
  encoding thread.

Both use synthetic 64x48 `testsrc2` video: four frames at 30 FPS, YUV420P,
no B-frames and GOP 30. Each Annex-B stream is extracted from its MP4 using
`h264_mp4toannexb` or `hevc_mp4toannexb` without re-encoding. Tests compare bytes
and access-unit counts within each generated pair, since compressed output can
vary between encoder versions.

## AV1

`internal/testdata/stream.ivf` contains six 64x48 Main 8-bit frames at 30 FPS,
with keyframes at indices 0 and 3. libaom-av1 encodes an RGB gradient, where
`frame` is the zero-based frame index:

```text
R = (x * 3 + frame * 18) % 256
G = y * 4
B = (x + y + frame * 12) % 256
```

IVF is the test container; the application transports its OBU payloads.

## AirPlay URL and HLS playback

`internal/testdata/url/` uses two seconds of synthetic 64x48 `testsrc2`
video at 10 FPS: H.264, YUV420P, GOP 10 and two B-frames. Audio is stereo
440 Hz AAC-LC at 44100 Hz and 64 kbit/s.

- `movie.mp4` uses faststart.
- `movie.m3u8` and `segment*.ts` are stream-copy HLS VOD with one-second
  segments; `master.m3u8` exercises relative variant URLs.
- `fragmented.m3u8`, `init.mp4` and `fragment*.m4s` contain fragmented-MP4 HLS
  from the same movie.

## AAC-ELD and ALAC audio

The audio inputs are synthetic stereo S16LE PCM with amplitude 8000, a 440 Hz
left channel and a 660 Hz right channel. `afconvert` encodes the inputs into
MP4; the generator extracts raw packets from sample tables and prefixes each
packet with a big-endian uint16 byte count.

`internal/testdata/` contains:

- `tone.aaceld`: half a second of input at 44100 Hz, producing 47 AAC-ELD packets
  of 480 samples. AudioSpecificConfig is `f8 e8 50 00` (AOT 39, stereo).
- `tone.alac`: the first 64 ALAC packets at 44100 Hz, with 352 samples per
  packet and the final flush packet omitted. ALACSpecificConfig uses 352 frames
  and 16-bit stereo; `maxFrameBytes` and `avgBitRate` may be zero (unknown) at
  the receiver.

`internal/testdata/tone48.aaceld` uses half a second of input at
48000 Hz, producing 51 AAC-ELD packets of 480 samples. AudioSpecificConfig is
`f8 e6 50 00` (stereo).
